nodes.partnerMessage:
Deadbolt's on, register is balanced, and the espresso machine is finally quiet. It's just me, the cooling room, and the streetlights through the front window.

You actually followed me into the private feed, {PlayerName}. One thing before we get too comfortable: I don't do voice calls. Text works better for me. I like having a second to think, and I'm usually covered in coffee anyway.

So... you're stuck with my typing. Hope that's okay.

choices.choiceText: Honestly, text is a relief. I'd rather get to know you this way.
Fair enough. What batch are you loading tonight?
No calls? Sounds like you're hiding because you're socially awkward.
Why do you stay late here instead of going home?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you. I actually like that.

On apps, people treat texting like a waiting room before the 'real' conversation. I don't mind typing. Sometimes I write a sentence, stare at it, delete half of it, and send the boring version anyway. 😂

It feels more honest somehow.

choices.choiceText: It gives words a little more weight. What's on your mind tonight?
You don't seem like someone who says things without thinking.
Let's see if your coffee is as thoughtful as your philosophy.
Does the quiet ever get overwhelming after closing?
What does your little corner of the world look like when you're not working?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Ha. You'd be surprised. I make plenty of terrible impulse decisions. I once bought a box of expired film at an estate sale because the cardboard looked cool.

But yeah... with the things I actually care about, I take my time. Coffee, photographs, people. I don't like rushing any of them.

choices.choiceText: A refrigerator full of expired film sounds extremely on-brand for you.
Does old film even come out properly after that many years?
Film and sourdough in the same fridge sounds dangerous.

nodes.partnerMessage:
They're both labeled. Very clearly. 😂

I'm a little chaotic, not completely reckless. Although there was one morning where I grabbed the wrong jar and nearly used darkroom rinse water on a starter. Caught myself before I committed the crime.

choices.choiceText: That's the most niche kitchen disaster I've ever heard.
Please tell me you don't feed your experiments to customers.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Absolutely not. The weird stuff stays at home.

My customers get normal bread, normal coffee, and the comforting illusion that I know exactly what I'm doing.

choices.choiceText: Good. I was starting to worry about surviving a visit.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Look, vegetables have an expiration date. Good film sometimes just gets character. That's my story and I'm sticking to it. 😭

The older stock can get this soft, hazy look that I really like for portraits. It's unpredictable, but sometimes that works in your favor.

choices.choiceText: Have you ever used that film for a portrait of someone you actually cared about?
Show me what you're working on right now.
What changes in the emulsion as it ages?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Once. My grandfather.

He was sitting on the back porch in that old green cardigan he wore all the time, peeling an orange with a pocketknife. Nothing dramatic. Just him being himself.

My mom still has the print. That's probably the photo I'm most protective of.

choices.choiceText: You turned an ordinary moment into something your family gets to keep.
Do you ever take portraits of yourself?

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's what I love about photographs. People disappear, places change, shops close... and suddenly you have this little piece of evidence that says, no, this really happened.

I think I got into archives for the same reason.

choices.choiceText: That sensitivity is one of the things I like about you.
Okay, now I want to see the coffee side of this archivist brain.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Almost never. 😂

I know what to do when I'm behind the camera. In front of it, suddenly my hands don't belong to me and I forget how faces work.

I'd rather be the person noticing everyone else.

choices.choiceText: One day I'll take a portrait of you where you actually look at the camera.
Being the observer probably feels safer.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Maybe. But no weird beauty filters. No smoothing my skin until I look like a different person.

And you have to catch me when I'm not trying too hard. That's the only kind of photo I'd actually keep.

choices.choiceText: Deal. Now show me the roaster.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Exactly. Behind the camera, nobody asks you to explain yourself. You're just there to notice things.

Which is probably why it's a little strange having you ask me how I'm actually doing.

choices.choiceText: Then answer me. How are you actually doing tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It gets less predictable. More fog, less contrast, weird color shifts depending on how it was stored.

Sometimes I fight it. Sometimes I lean into it. That's the fun part.

Wait... are you actually interested in the chemistry, or are you just being nice to me?

choices.choiceText: I'm genuinely interested. You clearly know your craft.
I care because you care. That's enough for me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's a dangerously nice thing to say at 11:30 PM.

I think the reason I get so focused on details is because most of my day is just problem after problem. Equipment breaks, bills show up, customers need something. Chemistry is one of the few places where I can slow everything down.

choices.choiceText: What part of the business has been draining you lately?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thanks.

People sometimes assume this whole thing was handed to me because I work with coffee and old cameras. It wasn't. I worked night shifts for years before I could afford the roaster I wanted.

I don't regret it. I just get tired of explaining that it wasn't some cute little hobby.

choices.choiceText: You built this yourself. That's worth being proud of.
Night shifts for years sounds rough.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My older brother still calls the shop my 'vanity project.' 😂

He means well, I think. He just measures success very differently from me.

Sometimes that gets under my skin more than I want to admit.

choices.choiceText: You build something people can actually experience. That's different from a spreadsheet.
Family opinions hit differently. I get that.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'm absolutely putting 'spreadsheets vs. flavor' on the shop whiteboard now. 😂

He'd hate it.

Okay, that actually made me feel better. Let's get this batch going.

choices.choiceText: Show me the beans.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. Part of me still wants my family to walk in, try one cup, and just get it.

Instead they ask how the margins look.

I know they care. It just isn't always the kind of care I need.

choices.choiceText: I get it. You don't have to prove the whole dream to me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, you're going to make me soft before I've even started the roast.

I should probably warn you that I get sentimental very easily after midnight.

choices.choiceText: Then I'll stay up with you. Now show me the batch.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It was exhausting. Long shifts, flour everywhere, and getting home while everyone else was starting their morning.

But I'd sit outside on breaks and read photography books and think, 'Someday this has to be my life.'

So when I look around this place now, I try to remember the version of me who wanted it before it was real.

choices.choiceText: You actually built the life you kept thinking about.
That kind of persistence is impressive. I really admire it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sometimes I forget. Rent, repairs, inventory... they make it hard to zoom out.

Then I look at the old machine and remember that I used to dream about owning even half of this room.

Thanks for reminding me.

choices.choiceText: Text me whenever you forget. I'll remind you.
Now show me the Ethiopian lot.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Careful. I might actually take you up on that when something breaks at four in the morning.

I have a bad habit of pretending everything is fine until I can't pretend anymore.

choices.choiceText: Then don't pretend with me.
I'd rather know when things are rough.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. I'll remember that.

Now help me make a good decision before I overthink this roast too.

choices.choiceText: Show me the curve.

nodes.partnerMessage:
People usually call me stubborn before they call me determined. 😂

Maybe both are true.

But hearing you call it persistence instead of a personality flaw is... nice.

choices.choiceText: Then take the boots off for a minute. You've done enough for tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I like the shop better after everyone leaves.

During the day I'm hearing orders, grinders, the door opening every thirty seconds... at night it's just the machines cooling down and the street outside.

I can finally hear myself think.

choices.choiceText: Do you ever feel invisible during the day?
Does the quiet ever scare you a little?
They're paying your bills, so maybe just enjoy the quiet after.
What does your night look like after the doors are locked?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sometimes, yeah.

People look at the menu, order, tap their card, and leave. That's normal. I just notice when someone actually asks me something instead of treating me like part of the furniture.

You asking about this stuff is... nice.

choices.choiceText: You're definitely not furniture to me. Show me the roast profile.
Then I'll keep asking.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. Sunday nights especially.

That's when my brain starts asking stupid questions like, 'What if the shop stops working? What if people move on? What if I picked the wrong life?'

I know it's just anxiety talking. Doesn't mean it shuts up.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to solve your whole future tonight.
A little doubt is normal. It can keep you honest.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You make things sound simpler than they feel from inside my head.

I'm going to save that message for the next time I start spiraling before opening.

choices.choiceText: Save it. Now show me what you've got.

nodes.partnerMessage:
True. A little fear keeps me from getting lazy.

Okay, enough emotional damage. 😂 Let's talk coffee before I start overthinking that too.

choices.choiceText: Bring up the roast curve.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know you're trying to be practical, but that answer landed a little cold.

This place is my whole life. If I only saw it as a transaction, I would've quit years ago.

choices.choiceText: You're right. I was being cynical. I'm sorry.
I was kidding. You're taking this too seriously.
Whatever. It's just a job.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah... that's about where the conversation stops being interesting for me.

I don't want to be someone's novelty experience for the night.

Maybe. I just know what kind of conversation I enjoy, and this is it.

You don't have to like that. But making fun of it two minutes into the chat tells me enough.

choices.choiceText: I was teasing. Don't take it so personally.
Enjoy talking to your coffee beans.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read.

Junia has minimized the conversation.

choices.choiceText: Junia? You still there?
I crossed a line. I'm genuinely sorry.
Leaving people on read is childish.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read 18m ago.

[Typing...]

Junia has switched status to 'Roasting - Do Not Disturb'.

...I don't mind disagreement. I mind feeling like the things I care about are being treated like a joke.

We're okay if you're actually willing to talk to me.

choices.choiceText: I am. Show me the batch.
I was thoughtless. I want to understand you better.

nodes.partnerMessage: User '{PlayerName}' was removed from the private backroom by Junia.

Thanks.

I know specialty coffee can look pretentious from the outside. For me, though, a lot of it started with my uncle. The smell of roasted beans is tied to him, and I think I've held onto that harder than I realized.

So yeah. Some comments hit a little deeper than they probably should.

choices.choiceText: I get that. Tell me about the batch you're roasting tonight.
How long has it been since he passed?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Three years this November.

He had this laugh you could hear from the street. At night, when the shop is quiet, I still catch myself expecting to hear it from the back room.

That's probably part of why I stay late sometimes.

choices.choiceText: Then keep something of him here. Show me the roast.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Tonight's Ethiopian Yirgacheffe from Gedeb.

I'm aiming for a lighter roast because I want the fruit to stay noticeable instead of turning everything into generic 'coffee flavor.' Here's the curve before I charge the drum.

choices.choiceText: That profile should let the blueberry and jasmine notes stay pretty clear.
Doesn't stretching the dry phase risk flattening the cup?
Why this lot in particular?
Can I taste it with you, even from here?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It can, yeah. That's why I watch the rate of rise instead of blindly following the same profile every time.

I know I get a little nerdy about this stuff, but the small changes are the whole point.

choices.choiceText: Okay, you know your machine. I respect that.
What made you settle on that drum speed?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Mostly trial and error. I kept changing the speed until the beans moved evenly without sitting in one hot spot.

You're either a coffee nerd or you're doing a really convincing impression of one. 😂

choices.choiceText: Just a coffee nerd who likes listening to you talk about it.
I like learning things from people who care about them.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Well... that's distracting. 😂

I'm trying to watch a roast curve and now I'm sitting here smiling at my phone.

Give me a second to pretend I still have professional composure.

choices.choiceText: Focus on the batch. I'll be here when it drops.
Take your time. What is the rate of rise doing?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Burner's backed off. Airflow's open.

...okay. First crack.

It always sounds louder than I expect. And the smell changes so fast. Sweet, fruity, a little like toasted sugar.

choices.choiceText: Pull the sample trier. Let's see where the color is.
I like hearing you get excited about this.

nodes.partnerMessage:
*metal scraping against the sample tray*

Color looks even. Chaff is clearing.

And... drop.

There it goes. The cooling tray is loud as hell for about ten seconds. 😂

choices.choiceText: You nailed it, Junia.
Step away for a second and breathe.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think we did.

It was weirdly nice having someone following along while I was doing it. Usually I finish a batch and the first thing I do is find another problem to fix.

Tonight I actually want to just enjoy it for a minute.

choices.choiceText: Then enjoy it. You earned that moment.
What would your uncle say about this batch?

nodes.partnerMessage:
*long exhale*

Okay. Sitting down.

My shoulders were way tighter than I realized.

I forget sometimes that I don't have to stay standing just because the work is still there.

choices.choiceText: You did enough for tonight. Give yourself a minute.
Get some water too.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Drinking water. Happy? 😂

Honestly, I needed that.

You're annoyingly good at noticing when I forget basic things.

choices.choiceText: Someone has to look after the person looking after everyone else.

nodes.partnerMessage:
He'd probably taste it first and pretend not to be impressed.

Then he'd find one tiny thing to complain about so I didn't get too proud of myself. 😂

After that he'd ask why I was smiling at my phone this late.

choices.choiceText: And what would you tell him?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'd probably say, 'I met someone who actually listens when I talk about this stuff.'

He'd tease me for getting attached too quickly.

Then he'd tell me not to be stupid and let you disappear.

choices.choiceText: I'm not going anywhere, Junia.
What are you doing after the roast?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...You're serious, huh?

I thought this might just be a fun late-night conversation, but you're actually staying for the boring parts too.

choices.choiceText: Those are usually my favorite parts.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Exactly. That's the balance.

You can get really technical about it, but eventually you're still standing next to a hot machine waiting to see whether the beans taste good.

That's what I like. All the science in the world still ends with a cup.

choices.choiceText: And you make it sound easy.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A lot of trial and error, honestly. You learn what the machine is doing and then you learn when not to argue with it.

I'm still learning too.

choices.choiceText: Pull the trier. Let's see how the batch finished.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Because my uncle loved this lot.

We cupped it together once and he kept going back to the same cup. He said it reminded him of late summer fruit.

I bought more than I should have after that. I think part of me just wanted to keep the memory around.

choices.choiceText: You kept more than the coffee. You kept that moment.
Then let's do it justice tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Now I have to do the part I've been avoiding.

There's a roll of portraits from the docks sitting in my bag. One of the people in it was Arthur, the older guy I told you about.

His daughter came by the shop last week and told me he passed away. I haven't developed the roll yet because I'm scared I messed it up.

choices.choiceText: Arthur, the guy with the wooden fishing lure?
Why not just trust the exposure you took?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. You remembered him.

He sat on the back of that old truck drinking coffee while I took a few frames. We ended up talking way longer than either of us expected.

If this roll came out badly, that's the part I'd be most upset about.

choices.choiceText: You were there. You remember the moment. The film doesn't get to erase that.
Stay in the chat while you develop it. I'll keep you company.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Because I was shooting into the morning light and there wasn't much room for mistakes.

I know the technical stuff. That's almost the problem. I can think of twenty ways I might have gotten it wrong.

choices.choiceText: Then stop thinking about the twenty ways. Trust the photo you took.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My hands are definitely less steady than I'd like.

I'm getting the chemicals ready and trying not to overthink the whole thing.

Stay here with me while I load the reel?

choices.choiceText: I'm here. Take your time.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Door's taped. Red light is on.

The room smells like fixer and wet cardboard. Very glamorous. 😂

I put my phone next to the enlarger so I can see your messages while I work.

choices.choiceText: Start the timer. I'll stay with you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. You're right.

Tank is loaded. Developer's in. Timer started.

I'm trying very hard not to stare at the clock every two seconds.

choices.choiceText: Then don't. Talk to me instead. How are you feeling?

nodes.partnerMessage:
*quiet rustling from the bag*

Film's on the reel. No buckling. Tank closed.

Okay. We're through the worst part. Developer is going in now.

choices.choiceText: Good. I'll keep you company while the timer runs.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Developer's in.

It's funny how slow eight minutes can feel when you're worried about something.

Usually I hate waiting. Tonight I don't mind it as much because I'm talking to you.

choices.choiceText: Then tell me something you don't usually tell people.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Minute four.

I'm trying not to obsess over the tank, so... confession time? I think part of me still hears my old art teacher whenever I work with film. She used to say digital had already won and I was wasting time learning a dead skill.

Maybe that's why I get so protective of it.

choices.choiceText: Maybe you don't have to prove anything to her anymore.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Minute six.

I'm getting ready for the stop bath.

And honestly? My hands stopped shaking a while ago. I think having someone to talk to made this way less scary than I expected.

choices.choiceText: Minute eight is coming. You've got this.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Eight minutes.

Developer out. Stop bath in. Fixer next.

Okay. Now we wait.

This is the worst part because there's nothing left to do except hope.

choices.choiceText: Then let's hope together.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Film's washed.

I'm holding the wet strip right now. It looks like a piece of plastic until I get it under the light.

...Give me a second.

choices.choiceText: Take your time. What do you see?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I see him.

His eyes are sharp. The steam is there. You can actually see the little lines around his smile.

I was so scared this would be the roll I ruined, and it's not.

I'm crying a little. Which is embarrassing, because I'm standing here in a rubber apron talking to my phone.

choices.choiceText: Don't be embarrassed. You preserved something that mattered to you.
Hang it up to dry. You did something beautiful tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The film is hanging to dry now.

I finally turned the red light off and went back into the main room.

The shop smells like coffee and rain again. Everything feels... quieter, but in a good way.

choices.choiceText: Sit down for a bit. You don't have to rush into the next thing.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I don't think I've heard 'I'm proud of you' in a long time without it being followed by a question about money or what I'm doing next.

You just stayed here. Even through the boring parts.

That means more to me than I expected.

choices.choiceText: I'm not going anywhere. I want the boring parts too.
Do you know what I like most about you?

nodes.partnerMessage:
The alley door is unlocked.

Coffee's cooling. Arthur's film is hanging on the line. The shop is finally quiet.

Come over, {PlayerName}.

No big speech. Just coffee, a chair, and an evening that doesn't need to be anything other than nice.

choices.choiceText: I'm putting my jacket on. Leave the light on.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Porch light's on.

French press is ready. I'm pretending I'm not checking the door every thirty seconds.

See you soon, favorite person.

Honestly? I'm tired.

The lease is going up, the drum bearing is making a noise I don't like, and I ruined a film test the other day because I was too cheap to buy more wetting agent.

Sometimes I wonder what my life would look like if I'd just picked the normal, stable option.

choices.choiceText: Then you wouldn't have this place, these prints, or this life you've built.
What went wrong with the film?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Ran out of Photo-Flo. Used a bad substitute. The roll came out with streaks everywhere. 😭

I knew better. I was just trying to save ten dollars and paid for it with two hours of work.

Please tell me you don't think I'm a genius after that.

choices.choiceText: I still think you're pretty impressive. Show me the coffee instead.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's the thing.

When first crack happens, even for a minute, I stop thinking about rent and broken equipment and whether I'm doing enough.

It's just the roast. That's probably why I keep coming back to it.

choices.choiceText: Then let's have one good minute tonight. Show me the curve.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'm so used to being the one who handles everything.

If something breaks, I fix it. If someone needs help, I show up. It's weird hearing someone say I deserve care too.

I'm not very practiced at receiving it.

choices.choiceText: Then you can practice with me. Start by showing me the roast.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay.

You've officially made it very hard for me to keep pretending this is just a fun little chat.

I'm going to unlock the alley door. Coffee's still warm. Come over.

choices.choiceText: On my way. Leave the light on.

nodes.partnerMessage:
After I close, I usually put on something quiet, wipe down the counter, and sit on the stool by the window for ten minutes.

No phone. No customers. Just breathing for a bit.

choices.choiceText: That sounds peaceful. Can I sit there with you someday?
You finally give yourself ten minutes?

nodes.partnerMessage:
You can. But I'm warning you now, the stool is terrible and I refuse to buy a prettier one just for a date. 😂

We'd probably just sit there and judge people walking past.

choices.choiceText: Perfect. That's exactly my kind of date.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Ten minutes on a good night. I'm working on it. 😂

Sometimes I get five. Sometimes I get distracted cleaning something that wasn't even dirty.

choices.choiceText: I'll remind you to sit down.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, then that's officially on the list.

Quiet shop. Bad stool. Good coffee. You and me talking until one of us realizes it's way too late.

choices.choiceText: That sounds dangerously good.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah... I think I'd like that.

I'm usually pretty careful about who gets to see this side of me.

Tonight feels different.

choices.choiceText: Then let me stay a little longer.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Come on, then.

Private room, coffee still warm, film hanging to dry, and no pressure to perform.

I think that's a pretty good place to leave the app behind. ☕🎞️

You should see the wall behind my desk.

Contact sheets, old labels, little notes, receipts from places that don't exist anymore. None of it matches, and I refuse to organize it because somehow the mess is part of the archive.

choices.choiceText: I want to see it. Show me the wall.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You say that now. Give it five minutes and you'll realize there are three layers of paper covering the same shelf. 😂

Still... I'd like showing it to you.

choices.choiceText: Then show me everything you're proud of.

nodes.partnerMessage:
There's a cup cooling beside me right now.

I keep wondering what you'd make of it. Not the technical notes. Just whether you actually like it.

choices.choiceText: Pour me one and I'll tell you honestly.
I trust the roaster. Surprise me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I like that answer.

Okay. One cup, no sugar first. Then you can complain to me afterward if I'm wrong. 😂

choices.choiceText: Deal. Coffee date officially scheduled.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You know what I've realized tonight?

I can talk about coffee or cameras for hours, but what actually makes me happy is the small stuff. Someone remembering what I said. Someone asking if I got home okay. Someone sitting nearby without needing anything.

choices.choiceText: I can do small things. I think those matter most.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Then maybe we're looking for the same kind of thing.

Not fireworks every five minutes. Just something steady that keeps feeling good.

choices.choiceText: I'd like to see where steady takes us.
